comment: So much busy work literally 12+ hours weekly outside of class. All about Neanderthals and ancient humans. Dr. Yang is a very nice person but underestimates how long her assignments take. "Flexible grading" actually just results in a million revisions and MORE work. Do not take this class unless you have a ton of time on your hands.

Big Data in Biology. Explained things well, very accessible outside of class, and told you exactly what you did wrong. Grade is determined by how much work you put in, so in order to get an A-/A, you have to put in a lot of time. Her lectures are pretty engaging and hw readings were relatively straightforward
I wouldn't. Too much for bio 199. Not a bad teacher tho. Pls save yourself the trouble. Pick a different bio 199.

Sweet person, difficult professor. She makes it clear how to get the grade you want in the class, but what isn't so clear is how much time that is going to cost you. No matter what letter grade you're aiming for, this class will have to become your #1 priority in order to even pass. Want even an A-? Good luck to you.

Dr. Yang is a great professor and sweet person, however the workload of her BIOL199 class is just INSANE. The work to get even an A- or B+ is too much and will take up probably 90% of all of your time. There's also just so many useless assignments. Please listen to all these reviews; save your time and take this class with another professor.

Dr. Yang cares about her students and provides excellent feedback on all assignments because of the nature of the class (specifications-based grading). You can resubmit assignments a few times and her feedback makes it really easy to edit things. Extremely helpful during office hours too.

Big Data w/ Dr. Yang is a difficult class, so if you are looking for an easy A this class is not for you. If you are willing to put in the work, however, this class is extremely rewarding. You will get lots of practice writing biology papers and a good grade is possible if you do all the assignments to satisfaction. The lab is quite boring tbh.

Dr. Yang is one of the nicest and most accessible professors at UR who truly cares about all her students. Her mastery type grading system makes it possible for all to succeed, but it takes a ton of time to do the work for a good grade. I learned a lot, but probably could have learned just as much with less effort in a traditional grading system.

I would not recommend taking this professor. This class will tank your GPA. Her grading system makes it extremely difficult to do well. Office hours do not help at all. It takes at least 20 hours of work per week outside of class, and even after putting in the hours, I got a C+ in the class. Good Luck :)

Wayyyy to much work for this class. She is a really nice teacher but all of this class is individual work that doesnt really pertain to the lecture at all. Labs are brutal you fill out a worksheet from a computer program for all three hours. Revisions help the grade but make it so much work.

Gives a lot of material, but is organized and clear with deadlines, making students able to manage their own time. Course helps develop important skills you will use in future biology courses. Very kind, and quick to respond emails and organize office hours.

Dr. Yang has something called CP (Challenge Problem) and CQ (Cumulative Quiz), all of them can be revised as long as they are completed. You get one chance free to revise, before this oral revision (or not) you can always schedule an office hour with her to further discuss your confusion or questions that you don't understand or know how to answer.
Unclear grading system and too much work

This class has wayyyyyyy too much work. She uses a unique grading system which makes it easier to attain a grade you want, however you will always have work to do. This class was a bit unorganized and not your regular biology class. You are expected you know a lot more than what is reasonable. I would only take this class if you are willing to work

I LOVE professor yang. She is passionate and always available to help. HOWEVER, this class is SO much work. It is revision-based, so you end up having to do most assignments again. The work really piles up. This class was more work than the rest of my classes combined. By the end of the semester, it got really exhausting. An A takes a lot of work.

Biol200 in general is a tough class, but Dr. Yang is a good professor! She does give a lot of work and grades pretty tough. Time management is essential for this class. Go to her office hours and show her that you care about your grade. Overall a really good professor!

Dr. Yang is a great professor! She gives a lot of work and grades pretty tough, but the work is really helpful. She also really cares about her students and is willing to make sure everyone understands the professor. A tough class, but as long as you put in the work you'll be fine. Overall a really good professor!

Lots of homework. I mean LOTS. Manageable, to *some* extent, but LOTS. Otherwise shes a really awesome person who knows her stuff and works hard for us, but she will make you work hard for her. Be ready to work hard for her.

Bio 200 is hard, but Dr. Yang wants to make it as easy as possible for her students. This doesn't mean less work, but you can always reach out to her directly and if you're not comfortable with that she lets you know where else you can get help. Take Dr. Yang!

@ the first review.... you're slacking <3 yes she gives a lot of work but that's bio 200 as a course, not really reflective of Dr. Yang. she wants students to genuinely understand the material-- if you go to her with questions she is extremely helpful. get to know dr. yang... she's funny af and wants to know where you feel you need extra help
She is disorganized. She is a new teacher and doesn't understand how to effectively teach. I love biology but I hated biology in her class. Also, she grades EVERYTHING.

Taking this course with Dr. Yang has pretty much destroyed my love of biology. All of the learning must be done on your own time with the textbook because lectures are all over the place and cover very little of what we need to know. On top of a heavy amount of reading, homework assignments are very long and feel almost entirely like busywork.
